chunks: The one who accuses a foundling of fornication is subjected to the prescribed punishment. And if a woman accuses her husband of fornication while he is deaf, they are separated, then she is never lawful for him again.

key_terms.اَللَّقِيطِ: a foundling; a child of unknown parentage who has been found
key_terms.قَاذِفُ: one who makes a slanderous accusation of fornication
key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ أَبَدًا: she is never lawful for him again
key_terms.يُحَدُّ: is subjected to the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slandering a foundling or a deaf husband in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning slanderous accusation (qadhf). It affirms the hadd punishment for accusing a foundling of fornication and rules that if a woman accuses her deaf husband, the spouses are separated and she never becomes lawful for him again.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5072 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The one who accuses a foundling (laqiṭ) of fornication is subjected to the prescribed punishment (hadd). And if a woman accuses her husband of fornication while he is deaf, they are separated, and she is never permissible for him again."
